title: Why Kindness is Your Competitive Edge in Leadership and Life
author: Heather McGonigal and Barbara Schindler
summary: In this written recap of a podcast episode, coaches Heather McGonigal and Barbara Schindler argue that kindness toward yourself and your team is a practical leadership tool for leaders running on pressure. They note that the nervous system registers extreme good news and extreme bad news with the same intensity, so a team member who seems too quiet or too fast may simply be carrying too much energy. Culture is what new hires see leaders actually do, including whether a supervisor ever takes a break, so announcing a short step away makes rest normal for everyone. Each coach shares a reset question, and a restaurant story shows how a calm remark can break a frenzy. The post closes with takeaways, an action list and reflection questions.
points: The authors say new employees judge whether a culture is healthy by what leaders demonstrate, including whether the supervisor ever takes a break.
Extreme good news and extreme bad news register in the body with the same intensity, which can explain a quiet or frantic team member.
Normalizing a visible pause, such as a message about stepping away for five minutes, makes rest safe for the whole team.
A back-pocket question like 'Am I calm?' interrupts reaction before it takes over, and calm gives you a choice about how to express frustration.
Burning through people and replacing them is described as short-term thinking about the whole business.
quotes: New employees decide whether a culture is healthy by watching what actually gets demonstrated, including whether their supervisor ever takes a break.
Calm does not erase frustration or anger; it gives you the choice of how to express it.
Your mind calls one bad and one good, while your body just registers extreme.
If that is normal, then Joe saying “I just got out of that meeting, I need five” is no big deal.
Culture is what people see you do, especially when you are under deadline.
Burning through people and replacing them is short-term thinking about your entire business.
A team that recharges while it works, like a Prius battery charging on the road, outlasts a team that runs until empty.
